newsitem.title: USA: SCANA signs 6-yr pact with Orangeburg.
newsitem.headline: SCANA signs 6-yr pact with Orangeburg.

text.p: South Carolina Electric & Gas Co said it signed a new six-year electricity supply agreement with the Orangeburg Department of Public Utilities to provide it with an initial capacity of 140 megawatts of electricity.
The agreement has been filed with the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission for final approval, the utility said.
Orangeburg DPU is the largest municipal electric utility system in South Carolina, the SCANA Corp subsidiary said.

"SCE&G has been able to sign its largest wholesale customer to an extended contract that will allow the company to sell more kilowatt-hours of electricity," president Jack Skolds said. "DPU will receive assured, reliable service at a rate that is 8.8 percent below the current contract rate."
The proposed agreement calls for SCE&G to provide DPU with its total electric needs for the first four years of the contract through April 30, 2001, the utility said.
This represents a six month extension over the October 2000 expiration for the contract it replases, a spokesman said.
Under the new contract, he said, Orangeburg pays for the contracted capacity whether it uses the power or not and can purchase additional power at any time.

The contracted demand level is set each year based on Orgeburg's forcasted load, the spokesman said, adding the level is expected to increase in the final three years of the firm contract based on Orangeburg's traditional demand growth of 2 to 3 percent per year.
The final two years of the contract call for SCE&G to provide 100 megawatts of electric capacity with the ability to provide more, the company said.
This represents a contract extension for SCE&G, the spokesman noted.
The company said the contract also includes an "Evergreen" clause that allows the contract to be automatically extended after six years.
Orangeburg submitted a request for proposals to receive electric service in October 1996. A total of 16 bids were submitted, the utility said.
